disposition: refused (design section 14.2, tenancy): the dialect is built, tested and measured at L1, L2 and L3 excellent against Jinja's own parser and template lookup (jinja2 3.1.6, tier A: jinja2.meta.find_referenced_templates and the AST, calibration/oracles/jinja2-meta) on openstack/kolla 23.0.0 kolla/docker and openstack/kolla-ansible 23.0.0 ansible/roles (520 files, tags dialect, cathaysia/tree-sitter-jinja v0.5.0, Apache-2.0), but reads no level: throughput .34 MB per CPU-second against the 1.0 floor (tenancy is always required), so the dialect is not dispatched and .j2, .jinja and .jinja2 stay disclosed as unsupported. Cause: the grammar lexes template text one character per token (`_words` is a repeat of single-character regexes), so a text-only file parses at about .4 MB per CPU-second and an expression-heavy one at .25; the pre-parse step (a text line's `# ` blanked, `in` and `not in` read as `==` and `!=` outside a for header) mends 75 of the 96 files that error as written, so files_with_error is 21 of 520 (4.04%, under the 5% line; kolla-ansible alone 19 of 331, 5.74%). Trigger: a Jinja grammar that lexes text as one token or an engine change that parses this grammar above 1.0 MB per CPU-second on the two subjects; then dispatch (an ExtractorEpoch bump), add the sniff for templates/*.html (the pipeline dispatches .html by extension before any sniff), and re-measure.
